question.worked_solution:
The "square of a sum" formula states that

$$
{n}^{2}+2an+{a}^{2}=(n+a)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
{n}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}n+\frac{25}{16}.
$$

First, we write the constant term as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}n+{(\frac{5}{4})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}^{2}+2\cdot \frac{5}{4}n+{(\frac{5}{4})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of sum formula with $a=\frac{5}{4}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{(n+\frac{5}{4})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
